# Alpha calibration: false alarms and power

Generated by scripts/alpha_calibration.py — do not edit.

Each trap and each honest twin of the A15 zoo (`tests/zoo/alpha_cases.py`) was generated with 20 seeds (40 symbols, 1000 business days unless a case needs more) and run through `validate_alpha` with 60 placebos and an AUM of 1e6. *Power* is the share of trap runs where the named check gave one of the statuses that count as caught (see the case list in the test file); a *false alarm* is a twin run where the same check did not give its expected quiet status. Intervals are Wilson 95 %. Targets: power at least 90%, false alarms at most 5% (judged on the point estimate).

## How to read this

The traps and twins are synthetic and were written by the maintainers; the numbers measure how the checks behave on these generators at this signal strength, not on real markets. A check with a statistical test (`signal_placebo`, `synthetic_market_null`) has a false-positive rate set by its own threshold (p above 0.10 fails a score with no edge), so its power on a pure-noise score cannot exceed about 90 % by design. Twins have a deliberately strong edge; with a weaker edge the checks that look at concentration (`universe_subsampling`) or at the t-statistic of the residual (`residual_alpha`) warn more often. With few seeds the intervals are wide: read the interval, not only the point.
